title: Casimir Force, Magnetization, and Susceptibility for \\ Ising Chain with an Impurity Atom in the Presence of an External Field
abstract: The article contains exact results for the behavior of the Casimir force of Ising chain of $N$ atoms containing an impurity atom. The force is considered as a function of $N$ and on both the temperature $T$ and the external magnetic field $h$. The interactions between nearest neighbors within the chain are supposed to be of a ferromagnetic short-ranged type $J>0$. The impurity atom interacts with constants $J_{ia}$ with its nearest neighbors, where $J_{ia}$ can be both of ferromagnetic type, i.e., $J_{ia}>0$, as well as of antiferromagnetic type, i.e., $J_{ia}<0$. It turns out that the Casimir force can be both attractive or repulsive, depending on the sign and the magnitude of the ratio $J_{ia}/J$.
summary: This theoretical paper calculates the Casimir force, magnetization, and susceptibility for an Ising chain modified by an impurity atom under an external magnetic field. Using the transfer matrix method, the authors show that the Casimir force's nature (attractive or repulsive) depends critically on the ratio of impurity to bulk coupling constants. This work provides detailed insights into finite-size effects in 1D quantum magnets.
main_problem: The paper determines the Casimir force, magnetization, and susceptibility for an Ising chain containing an impurity atom under an external magnetic field.
main_result: The Casimir force can be either attractive or repulsive, depending on the sign and magnitude of the ratio of the impurity interaction to the nearest-neighbor coupling constant. The analysis also provides scaling functions for the force.
method: The calculations utilize the transfer matrix method to find the partition function, from which the free energy, Casimir force, magnetization, and susceptibility are derived.
model_or_system: The system is a one-dimensional Ising chain of N spins ($S_i = \pm 1$) with a specific Hamiltonian that includes nearest-neighbor interactions ($J>0$) and an impurity interaction ($J_{ia}$).
key_observables: Casimir force ($ eta F_{	ext{Cas}}$), Magnetization ($m$), and Susceptibility ($\chi$).
important_parameters: Chain length ($N$), temperature ($T$), external magnetic field ($h$), and coupling constants ($J, J_{ia}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis involves decomposing the free energy into bulk, surface, and finite-size correction terms, and deriving scaling functions in the large N limit.
figures_summary: Figures show the susceptibility ($\chi$) and the Casimir force ($ eta F_{	ext{Cas}}$) as functions of the external field $h$ and coupling constants, illustrating symmetry and scaling behavior.
paper_structure: The paper calculates the partition function via the transfer matrix, derives the free energy density, and then uses this to analytically determine the Casimir force, magnetization, and susceptibility, often presenting results in scaling forms.
why_interesting: The study of boundary effects (Casimir force) and impurity effects in 1D quantum spin chains is fundamental to understanding finite-size corrections and local perturbations in many-body quantum systems.

There are interaction bonds between any two spins equal either to J, or to Jia. In the depicted example we have 8 spins +1, and 12 spins −1. The last implies that the total magnetization of the chain is M = ∑20 i=1 Si = −4.
FIGURE 2. The behavior of the average magnetization for K = 3 and K = −3 for a chain with N = 20 random (dynamical) variables.

FIGURE 3. As we see, the susceptibility is symmetric with respect of the sign of the external magnetic field h. In the current figure the left panel shows that for relatively small N one has a single minimum in a chain in which the impurity atom interacts in a way similar to the rest of the chain (i.e., in a ferromagnetic way; Kia=3), while in the opposite case, Kia = −3, it has two maxima. The right panel: for relatively large N the both functions are very similar.

FIGURE 4. As we see, the force is always symmetric with respect of the sign of the external magnetic field h. In the current figure the left panel shows the behavior of the Casimir force for N = 100 with Kia = 3. The right panel depicts the behavior of the Casimir for again N = 100 but for Kia = −3. The behavior of the force is shown as a function of K and h.
